The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-2$ | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $5$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-2$ | $-2$ | $0$ |
|  | $1$ | $1$ | $0$ | $5$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+2x+5}{x+2}={x}^{2}+x+\frac{5}{x+2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+2x+5}{x+2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+x+\frac{5}{x+2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+5{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1}+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}+5(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{3}{2}\,).\end{aligned}
$$
